**Finding: COMPLIANT (preferred position) — no redline proposed.**

- **No minimum/take-or-pay anywhere:** the term "minimum" does not appear in the document; no purchase commitment, minimum royalty, or volume cap on Ono.
- **Supply is a right, not an obligation:** §9.4(a) gives Ono "the right (but not the obligation)" to manufacture or subcontract its own requirements; §9.4(b) gives Ono the *right* to obtain commercial requirements from Array; §9.3(a) supply is only "as reasonably requested in writing by Ono." Forecasting/ordering mechanics are deferred to future clinical and commercial supply agreements.
- **Payments are event- or usage-based:** upfront licence fee, milestones on first achievement, and royalties on actual Net Sales (§6.3).
- **The only "shortfall" (§6.3(c)) is a year-end royalty reconciliation true-up** on actual sales — precisely the true-up mechanic the fallback contemplates, not a penalty.
- Any requirements-sourcing angle would fall under exclusivity, not MINCOMMIT, and in any event Ono is expressly free to self-manufacture or use a subcontractor.

Watch-item noted for the negotiation team: re-test this rule when the clinical and commercial supply agreements are drafted, since binding forecast/order terms there could introduce a commitment.
